questions.prompt: Which change is most likely to be backward-compatible when designed carefully?
options: Changing the meaning or type of an existing response field in place.
Removing an endpoint that still has active supported clients.
Adding an optional response field while preserving existing fields and behavior, after checking client assumptions.
Renaming a required property without coordinating with consumers.
questions.answer_key: Adding an optional response field while preserving existing fields and behavior, after checking client assumptions.
questions.explanation: Adding an optional response field while preserving existing fields and behavior, after checking client assumptions. This is especially relevant to “API Change Management” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “API Change Management”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Compare old and new contracts and test an existing consumer before rollout.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
questions.answer_key: Compare old and new contracts and test an existing consumer before rollout.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “API Change Management”?
options: A breaking change is shipped without usage data, migration guidance, or a deprecation plan.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
questions.answer_key: A breaking change is shipped without usage data, migration guidance, or a deprecation plan.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
